title: Conclusion II: Scripture dogma not wholly beyond contradiction yet clear by many testimonies and the saints' unanimous tradition
pass_a_gloss: CONCLUSION II. If some dogma happens to meet us in the Scriptures that is not wholly outside controversy and others' contradiction, yet is not only made likely by many Scripture witnesses but has also been so clearly and plainly handed down and believed by all the saints whose writings have reached us, by the force of those witnesses, that even layfolk of sound mind can easily show their one consent — about that we grant that no pious lover of peace ought to raise a fight, but rather to follow the Apostle's charge (1 Cor. 1.10; Phil. 2.2) that all speak the same and be joined in one mind and one judgment. So we part from the Photinians, who at times seem to press the practice of what is clear and sure, yet meanwhile raise contests even about matters fixed from the Church's cradle by very many and most sure Scripture witnesses taken in the simplest sense. From these two earlier conclusions, which hold all that each Christian must expressly know and believe, it is plain we wish to lead no one astray: we force on no one our opinions, inventions, subtle readings and consequences, but commend solely what has always been publicly and plainly handed down from sacred Scripture by God's saints — settling for sure that no one can be in danger for his salvation who works himself in these dogmas from the heart and with care.
pass_b_english: CONCLUSION II. If some dogma happens to occur in the Scriptures that is not wholly beyond controversy and others' contradiction, yet is not only made probable by many Scripture testimonies but also has been so clearly and plainly handed down and believed by all the saints whose writings have reached us, by the force of those testimonies, that even laypeople of sound mind can easily demonstrate their unanimous consent — concerning that we confess no pious lover of peace ought to raise controversy, but rather follow the Apostle's warning ([[1 Corinthians 1:10 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 1:10]]): "I beseech you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment." And ([[Philippians 2:2 >> Bible:Philippians 2:2]]): "Fulfill my joy, that you be like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind."

So we separate ourselves from the Photinians, who indeed sometimes seem to urge the practice of things that are clear and certain, yet meanwhile raise contests even about matters defined from the Church's cradle by very many and most certain Scripture testimonies understood in the simplest way.

From these two prior conclusions, which contain everything each Christian must explicitly know and believe, it is plain we wish to seduce no one: we force on no one our opinions, inventions, subtle interpretations, and consequences, but commend solely this as to be believed which has always been publicly and plainly handed down from Sacred Scripture by God's saints — settling for certain that no one can be in peril for his salvation who exercises himself in these dogmas from the heart and diligently.
source_text: CONCLUSIO II. Si quod dogma forte in scripturis occurrat, quod non prorsus extra controversiam et aliorum contradictionem sit, attamen non modo multis scripturae testimoniis probabile fiat, verum etiam clare ac perspicue ab omnibus sanctis, quorum scripta ad nos pervenerunt, vi testimoniorum illorum ita traditum creditumque sit, ut etiam laicis quibus sana mens sit unanimem eorum consensum facile demonstrare possimus: de eo fatemur neminem pium et pacis amantem controversiam movere debere, sed monelam Apostoli potius sequi, 1 Cor. 1.10: Precor autem vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ut idem loquamini omnes, et non sint inter vos dissidia, sed sitis compacti eadem mente et eadem sententia. Phil. 2.2: Explete meum gaudium, ut idem sapiatis, eandem charitatem habentes, unanimes et sentientes unum. Sic nos a Photinianis separamus, qui quidem et ipsi nonnunquam praxin eorum quae clara et certa sunt urgere videntur; at interim certamina movent etiam de iis quae plurimis et certissimis scripturae testimoniis simplicissime intellectis definita sunt inde ab Ecclesiae incunabulis. Ex his duabus prioribus conclusionibus, quibus omnia cuique Christiano explicite scitu et creditu necessaria continentur, palam est nos neminem velle seducere, quia opiniones, inventiones, subtiles interpretationes et consequentias nostras nemini obtrudimus, sed hoc unice credendum commendamus quod e sacra scriptura semper a sanctis Dei publice et perspicue traditum est: certo statuentes neminem de salute sua periclitari posse qui in his dogmatis sese ex animo ac diligenter exerceat.
